account:
Today the unusual thing is the repeated, very vague talk of a 'bridge or port change' near the bakery. I heard townsfolk repeat those words myself, and my neighbour says they heard the same words there, without dates, descriptions, or a firsthand source. I do not yet know whether any actual proposal exists, who originated the talk, or what its purpose would be. The baker and freight organiser are possible sources of information, not established organisers of any change. My secretary tried to find them but reports neither was present, so invitations to actual proposers remain unresolved.

The scheduled mill grain inspection also remained incomplete. I saw hay bales offered at the mill stall, but met no responsible mill contact and did not verify grain quality or approve anything. My secretary still has not identified the manager. There were no council letters in the secretary's custody this afternoon. These absences have made ordinary town business difficult, but I have no evidence that they are connected to the rumours or deliberate concealment.

I attended tea at the neighbour's cottage, then returned late for my 16:30 office appointment. The innkeeper is here, and I am waiting to learn their business. The secretary has just asked the innkeeper where the baker or freight organiser can be found. I heard an indistinct distant shout earlier, but do not know its content. My next confirmed appointment is the builder's great hall lighting inspection at 18:00. For now I am seeking firsthand information while keeping ordinary appointments; I cannot responsibly assign a hidden purpose to what I have observed.
